title: Minimum Cost to Make Array Equalindromic
statement:
You receive an integer array `nums`. A single move adds 1 to, or subtracts 1 from, one element of your choice.

Find the fewest moves after which all elements hold one common value `p` that is a positive palindrome: an integer `p >= 1` whose decimal digits read identically from left to right and from right to left (for example `7`, `44` or `1221`). Return that number of moves.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every palindrome as the common value works but there are about 10^5 of them below 10^9. Look at the total cost `sum |x - p|` as a function of the target `p`: it falls until `p` reaches the median of `nums` and rises after it. So among palindromes, only two can win: the largest one not above the median and the smallest one not below it.

Those two can be built directly from the median's digits. Any palindrome is fixed by its first half, so the nearest ones of the same length come from mirroring the median's first half, or that half minus one or plus one. A change of length gives two more: `99...9` with one digit fewer and `10...01` with one digit more.

## Approach

1. Sort a copy of `nums` and take `median`, the middle element (either middle works for an even length).
2. Take the first `half` of its `digits` and note whether the length is `odd`.
3. `mirror(head)` appends the reversed head (without its last digit when the length is odd), which always gives a palindrome.
4. Build the five `candidates`: `10^(L-1) - 1`, `10^L + 1`, and the mirrors of `half - 1`, `half` and `half + 1`.
5. Keep `below`, the largest positive candidate `<= median`, and `above`, the smallest candidate `>= median`.
6. Return the smaller of `cost(below)` and `cost(above)`.

## Example 1, step by step

Sorted `nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]`, so `median = 3`, a single odd digit with `half = 3`. The candidates are `0, 11, 2, 3, 4`, so `below = 3` and `above = 3`. `cost(3) = 2 + 1 + 0 + 1 + 2 = 6`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort; the candidates take O(number of digits) and each cost is O(n).
- Space: O(n) for the sorted copy.

## Pitfalls

- With an even length, the cost is flat between the two middle values; using one middle value still works because `below` and `above` bracket it.
- Mirroring `half - 1` can give `0`, which is not positive, so it must be skipped.
- Near powers of ten (`1000`, `999`) the nearest palindrome has a different length, which is why `99...9` and `10...01` are candidates.
- The answer can reach about 10^14 on LeetCode's limits, so Java and C need a 64-bit total.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `sorted`, `median` | sorted copy of `nums` and its middle element |
| `digits`, `odd` | the median as text, and whether its length is odd |
| `half` | the first half of the median's digits, as a number |
| `mirror` | turns a first half into the palindrome it determines |
| `candidates` | the palindromes that can be nearest to the median |
| `below`, `above` | nearest palindrome not above and not below the median |
| `cost`, `total` | moves needed to bring every value to a target |
